problem_description: Docker container keeps getting killed with exit code 137. The OOMKilled flag is set to true in docker inspect output.
solution: Exit code 137 means the container was killed by the OOM (Out of Memory) killer. Increase the container memory limit using --memory flag or in docker-compose.yml. Check your application for memory leaks. For JVM apps, set -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.

problem_title: Fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories
problem_description: When trying to pull or merge, git throws 'fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories' error.
solution: Use the --allow-unrelated-histories flag: git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories. This happens when two repos with different root commits are being merged, commonly after a force push or when combining two separate projects.

problem_description: Getting AccessDeniedException when trying to upload files to S3 bucket even though IAM policy seems correct.
solution: Check for: 1) Bucket policy conflicting with IAM policy, 2) S3 Block Public Access settings, 3) The IAM role/user ARN matches what's in the bucket policy, 4) If using KMS encryption, ensure kms:GenerateDataKey permission is granted, 5) Check for explicit Deny statements that override Allow.

problem_description: Package installs successfully with pip but Python throws ModuleNotFoundError when trying to import it.
solution: This usually means pip and python point to different environments. Fix: 1) Use 'python -m pip install package' to ensure same environment, 2) Check 'which python' and 'which pip' point to same location, 3) If using virtualenv, make sure it's activated, 4) For multiple Python versions, use python3 -m pip explicitly.

problem_description: Getting 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock' error when running docker commands.
solution: 1) Start Docker daemon: sudo systemctl start docker, 2) Add user to docker group: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER (then logout/login), 3) Check if Docker Desktop is running (macOS/Windows), 4) Check socket permissions: ls -la /var/run/docker.sock
error_pattern: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon

problem_title: ENOSPC: System limit for file watchers reached
problem_description: Node.js dev server crashes with ENOSPC error about file watchers when running in watch mode.
solution: Increase the inotify watch limit: echo fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288 | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf && sudo sysctl -p. This is a Linux kernel limit on how many files can be watched simultaneously.
error_pattern: ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached

problem_description: React component crashes on initial render when trying to .map() over data fetched from an API. Works after refresh sometimes.
solution: The data hasn't loaded yet on first render. Add a null check: data?.items?.map() or initialize state with an empty array. Use optional chaining or provide a default: (data.items || []).map(). Consider adding a loading state to prevent rendering before data arrives.

problem_description: Kubernetes pod keeps restarting and is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff status. The pod starts, runs for a few seconds, then crashes.
solution: 1) Check logs: kubectl logs pod-name --previous, 2) Describe the pod: kubectl describe pod pod-name, 3) Common causes: application crashes on startup, missing env vars or config maps, insufficient resources, failing health checks, 4) Check if the container command is correct, 5) Verify image exists and is pullable.

problem_description: Browser blocks API requests with CORS policy error. The request works in Postman but fails from the frontend.
solution: CORS is enforced by browsers, not by Postman. Fix on the backend: 1) Add Access-Control-Allow-Origin header for your frontend domain, 2) For Express: use cors() middleware, 3) For FastAPI: add CORSMiddleware, 4) For development, allow localhost origins, 5) Never use '*' with credentials in production.

problem_description: Bash script won't execute, getting 'Permission denied' even though the file exists and content is correct.
solution: The file doesn't have execute permission. Fix: chmod +x script.sh, then run with ./script.sh. If on a mounted filesystem (like NTFS), mount with exec option. If the shebang is wrong, check the first line is #!/bin/bash (no extra whitespace or BOM characters).

problem_title: Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'
problem_description: TypeScript compiler throws error when passing a possibly undefined value to a function that expects a definite string.
solution: You need to handle the undefined case. Options: 1) Non-null assertion: value! (only if you're sure), 2) Default value: value ?? 'fallback', 3) Type guard: if (value) { ... }, 4) Optional parameter: make the function accept string | undefined, 5) Use type narrowing with typeof check.

problem_description: After checking out a commit or tag, git says 'You are in detached HEAD state'. Changes might be lost.
solution: You checked out a specific commit instead of a branch. To keep your changes: 1) Create a new branch: git checkout -b new-branch-name, 2) Or switch back to a branch: git checkout main. If you already made commits in detached state, create a branch from current position before switching: git branch save-my-work.

problem_description: Python raises RecursionError when calling a function. The function works for small inputs but fails for larger ones.
solution: Your function has infinite or too-deep recursion. Fixes: 1) Check base case — make sure recursion actually terminates, 2) Convert to iterative approach using a stack/queue, 3) If recursion is correct but deep, increase limit: sys.setrecursionlimit(10000) (careful with memory), 4) Use memoization (@functools.lru_cache) to avoid recomputing.

problem_description: AWS Lambda function hits the maximum timeout (15 min) when processing large datasets. Need to handle larger workloads.
solution: Lambda has a hard 15-minute limit. Options: 1) Break work into smaller chunks using SQS + multiple Lambda invocations, 2) Use Step Functions for orchestration, 3) Move to ECS/Fargate for long-running tasks, 4) Optimize the function (parallel processing, reduce I/O waits), 5) Use Lambda's streaming response for gradual output.

problem_title: useEffect runs twice in development mode
problem_description: useEffect hook fires twice on component mount in React 18 development mode. API calls happen twice.
solution: This is intentional in React 18 Strict Mode. In development, React mounts, unmounts, and remounts components to help find bugs. It does NOT happen in production. Fixes: 1) Ignore it (it's dev-only), 2) Use a cleanup function in useEffect, 3) Use a ref to track if already fetched, 4) Remove StrictMode wrapper if it's blocking development (not recommended long-term).
